construction_evidence: Let U be the union of the stated G_beta classes, H={u:u_1=0}, Z_n={alpha_hat_n=0}, E_n={sqrt(n)X_1<=Phi^{-1}(1-gamma)}, and B_n the empirical-Bayes ball with fixed inflation L>=1 large enough for uniform conservative coverage. All truths in U lie in H; therefore P_theta(E_n)=1-gamma exactly. The existing coverage theorem supplies epsilon_n=sup_U P_theta(theta notin B_n)->0. It does not itself claim exact nominal coverage. For n<3 take the whole space; finite initial sample sizes do not affect any asymptotic target.

For completeness, uniformity of the Sobolev radius bound over beta is checked directly. Write q_alpha=1+2alpha+2p and N_alpha=n^(1/q_alpha). The normalized score h_n in the bracket lemma is at most R^2 N_alpha^{-min(1,2(beta-alpha))} for alpha<=beta, for all sufficiently large n uniformly over the compact beta interval. To see this, write e_i=i^(2beta)theta_i^2 with sum e_i<=R^2. For i<=N_alpha, the multiplier of e_i after dividing by N_alpha log N_alpha is bounded by N_alpha^{-min(1,2(beta-alpha))}. For i>N_alpha, use (i^q_alpha+n)^2>=i^(2q_alpha) and the decreasing function i^(-1-2alpha-4p-2beta)log i; its endpoint bound is N_alpha^{-2(beta-alpha)}. The coordinate i=1 contributes zero.

Choose a fixed D>0 with R^2 exp[-2D/(1+2beta_++2p)]<(16C^8)^(-1). For large n this score bound is below the lower-bracket threshold throughout alpha<=beta-D/log n. Hence underline_alpha_n>=a_{n,beta}:=beta-D/log n. The actual lower-selector bracket gives sup_{beta,theta in G_beta}P_theta(alpha_hat_n<a_{n,beta})->0. Since a_{n,beta}>=beta_-/2 eventually, this also gives delta_n=sup_U P_theta(Z_n)->0.

For a>=beta_-/2, sum_i (i^(1+2a)+n kappa_i^2)^(-1)<=K n^(-2a/(1+2a+2p)), by splitting at N_a. Below N_a, use C^2 i^(2p)/n and sum i^(2p)<=2N_a^(1+2p); above N_a use the summable tail i^(-1-2a), bounded uniformly because a>=beta_-/2 and a<=A. The centered posterior norm has this sum as its second moment, so its (1-gamma)-quantile squared is at most that sum divided by gamma. Each posterior variance, and thus this quantile, decreases in a. On alpha_hat_n>=a_{n,beta}, the selected radius is bounded by a constant times n^(-beta/(1+2beta+2p)), uniformly in beta, since the derivative of a/(1+2a+2p) is at most 1/(1+2p). Thus B_n has the required uniform stochastic no-log diameter, including its vanishing-probability whole-space branch.

Define C_n=ell^2 on Z_n; on Z_n complement put C_n=B_n on E_n and C_n=B_n minus H on E_n complement. The first posterior coordinate on alpha_hat_n>0 has variance (1+n kappa_1^2)^(-1)>0, so its probability of being zero, and thus its probability of H, is zero for every such data point. Removing H preserves B_n posterior mass, which is at least 1-gamma. It also cannot increase diameter. Borel coordinate maps, the measurable selector, the norm as a limit of partial sums, and Borel Gaussian norm quantiles give a measurable membership graph. On the positive-selector branch B_n has positive radius; B_n minus H is dense in B_n, so its diameter is exactly that of B_n. The diameter random variable is therefore measurable as well.

For every allowed truth, coverage of C_n is P_theta(Z_n)+P_theta(Z_n complement intersect E_n intersect {theta in B_n}). Subtracting P_theta(E_n)=1-gamma leaves P_theta(Z_n intersect E_n complement)-P_theta(Z_n complement intersect E_n intersect {theta notin B_n}). Its absolute value is bounded uniformly by delta_n+epsilon_n->0. No independence between E_n and B_n or the selector is needed. Diameter is bounded by that of B_n on every branch, and the zero-selector probability tends uniformly to zero. The norm lower bound m plays no role in this construction.
repair_notes.class_comparison_evidence: For any fixed positive M,R, theta_i^2=M i^(-1-2beta) belongs to the coordinatewise hyperrectangle but has infinite beta-Sobolev energy. A single coordinate theta_k^2=R^2 k^(-2beta) belongs to the Sobolev ellipsoid but has hyperrectangle seminorm R^2 k, exceeding M for large k. These witnesses show the two unrestricted regularity sets are incomparable; they do not claim that every possible fixed polished-tail intersection G_beta is incomparable with every hyperrectangle. For the actual sparse-gap truth, each disjoint block N_j<i<=2N_j has weighted energy M sum 1/i>=M/4 eventually, proving infinite beta-Sobolev energy. Long zero blocks followed by nonzero tails also violate every fixed polished-tail condition.
